text.p: Bulgarian opposition candidate Petar Stoyanov is leading with 61.3 percent in Sunday's presidential election run-off to 37.3 percent for Ivan Marazov of the governing Socialists, a projection based on actual results showed.
The projection was broadcast by private Darik radio quoting the Bulgarian Association for Fair Elections and Civil Rights (BAFE).
First official results are expected early on Monday and final results must be announced by Wednesday.
The Central Electoral Commission said about 50 percent of the electorate had voted by 4 p.m. (1400 GMT), slightly higher than last week's turnout.

Although the president has limited powers under Bulgaria's post-communist constitution, a big win for Stoyanov could severely weaken the Socialist government of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov, already under fire for its management of the economy.
